transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I just keep getting stuck on this... this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek. 

I notice it all the time in photos, and especially under the bright fluorescent lights at the store where I work. Even when I point it out to other people and they say they don't see it, it just feels like it's the very first thing customers and my managers notice when they look at me. It's just been really bothering me, so I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Do you find yourself doing anything specific to try to hide, fix, or constantly check this spot when you are at work or getting ready?

Yeah, I do. Um, when I'm on my breaks at work, I usually end up going to the bathroom just to check my face in the mirror. I try fixing my hair around it to sort of cover it up. And I definitely catch myself comparing myself to the girls who come through my checkout line. Sometimes I get so caught up in checking the mirror and messing with my hair that it takes a really long time, and I actually end up being late getting back to the register.
Do you ever find yourself picking, scratching, or rubbing at that spot on your skin in an attempt to make it look better or to remove it?

No, not really. I mean, I don't pick at it or scratch it. It's not really like a pimple or something that I feel like I can just scrape off, you know? It's more just... the shape of it, the way it looks. So, no, I don't rub at it or anything like that. I mostly just look at it in the mirror and try to cover it up.
How much does this concern about your appearance interfere with your ability to enjoy your time outside of work or maintain your relationships with friends and family?

Well, outside of work, it doesn't get in the way too much. I still see my friends and family just fine. But, um, it is definitely causing problems for me at my job. 

Like I said about the mirror checking... my manager has actually started noticing that I'm coming back from my breaks late. And I think I'm moving slower at the register, too, because I'm just so distracted by it. I'm really worried that it's making me look unreliable, especially right now because I'm trying to get promoted.
When you are away from a mirror and trying to focus on other tasks, how much of your time is spent thinking about or worrying about how this spot looks?

Um, when I'm away from a mirror... I'm not really sure how to put a number on it. I guess I think about it a fair amount, but it's not like it's the only thing in my head all day. I mostly just get distracted by it when I see someone else or if I feel like my hair moved and isn't covering it right anymore. But if I'm really busy ringing people up, I can focus on my work for a while without thinking about it too much.
Have you ever considered or sought out any medical or cosmetic procedures, such as seeing a dermatologist or a plastic surgeon, to try and fix or change the appearance of that spot?

No, I haven't really thought about anything like that. I don't think I'd go to a doctor or a surgeon for it. I just try to manage it myself by covering it up with my hair or makeup. I haven't looked into any procedures or anything.
